title: He had the power to kill him.
paragraphs:
He had the power to kill him.
But something inside him chose mercy.
The storm was not just outside the ship.

Inside fear.
Inside pride.
Inside survival instincts screaming, “Save yourself—even if someone else must die.”
Because if even one escaped… it would cost them their own lives.
That’s how brutal the system was.
That’s how cold the world can be.

Chained.
Powerless.
At the mercy of men who were one command away from ending his life.
Something unexpected broke through the storm.
A Roman centurion named Julius stood in the gap.
And in that moment, he faced a silent war inside his own chest.

Duty vs compassion.
Protocol vs conviction.
Power vs restraint.
And Scripture tells us what he chose:

“The soldiers planned to kill the prisoners…
But the centurion, wanting to save Paul, kept them from carrying out their plan.” — Acts 27:42–43

Not forced.
Not commanded.
Not pressured.
Most of us have stood on that same edge.
But in moments where we had the power to harm.
With decisions made in anger, pride, or fear.
We all carry the capacity to destroy.
To protect ourselves at the expense of others.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” — Romans 3:23
Including the one reading this right now.
But here’s where the story cuts deeper.
But Julius could not save Paul’s soul.
And neither can you save yourself.
Because the real storm is not outside.

The storm of sin.
The weight of guilt.
The quiet shame no one else sees.
The memories that replay at night.
The things you hope nobody finds out.
The moments you wish you could undo.
We want mercy when we fail…
But we want justice when others do.
But we struggle to give it.
But we think we can earn it.
And it came at a cost.
This is where the Gospel crashes into the storm.
Jesus Christ did not stand at a distance like Julius.
He stepped into the storm Himself.
But to rescue all who would believe.
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” — Romans 5:8
Jesus took the judgment we deserved.
“He himself bore our sins in his body on the tree…” — 1 Peter 2:24
Julius stopped soldiers from killing Paul.
Jesus stopped sin from killing you.
But only if you receive Him.
Because here’s the part many people avoid:
And it will cost you your pride.
You cannot hold on to your sin and hold on to Christ at the same time.
You cannot stay the same and follow Him.
You cannot say “Lord” and still be your own master.
“Repent therefore, and turn back, that your sins may be blotted out.” — Acts 3:19
Maybe you’ve been living like those soldiers.
Things no one sees—but God does.
Because the same God who moved a Roman centurion to show mercy…
Sent His Son to give you eternal mercy.
Jesus would not have gone to the cross.
Not as someone who has it all together.
But as someone who needs saving.
Because that’s the only kind of person He saves.
You won’t just survive the storm.
